text:
Today no one has come to ask;

nor have they asked anything of me this afternoon.


I have not seen a single cemetery flower

in so joyful a procession of lights.

Forgive me, Lord: how little I have died!


This afternoon everyone, everyone passes by

without asking me or asking anything of me.


And I do not know what they forget, and it remains

wrong in my hands, like something alien.


I have gone out to the door,

and I feel like shouting to everyone:

If you are missing something, it is left here!


Because on every afternoon of this life,

I do not know with what doors they strike a face,

and something alien takes over my soul.


Today no one has come;

and today, how little I have died this afternoon!

translation.title: Agape
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's paradox of unclaimed loss: something alien remains, and yet he has died only a little.
